review_rule: A Core identity is retained only when a payload schema, capability parameter, or separately versioned extension cannot replace the cross-boundary interaction grammar.

groups.name: abi_value_and_table_structures
groups.extension_impossibility: These are the memory, ownership, sizing, discovery, scene-revision, objective-envelope, and lease prefixes needed before any versioned payload can be interpreted. Internal SceneIR, RenderConfig, estimator, backend, and resource layouts are absent.
groups.evolution: Existing prefixes and successful semantics are immutable; compatible additions are tail-only and validated against the frozen 1.0 prefix size. New domains use new tables or schemas.

groups.name: result_and_error_grammar
groups.extension_impossibility: Bootstrap, table calls, and worker envelopes require one result vocabulary before extension discovery. Details remain versioned structured payloads.
groups.evolution: New detail uses structured error schemas; new universal outcomes append identities without changing existing numeric values.

groups.name: capability_axes_and_boundary_families
groups.extension_impossibility: Bootstrap, lifecycle, frame lease, native-scene fallback, and generic render-session availability correspond to the frozen calling families themselves. Algorithm, provider, format-feature, and research availability remains outside Core.
groups.evolution: Capability descriptors carry independent stability, maturity, runtime state, dependencies, limits, and reason data; optional functionality receives extension identities.

groups.name: core_events
groups.extension_impossibility: Operation state, frame readiness, loss/gap, diagnostics, and full-scene revision replacement are required to coordinate the stable asynchronous lifetimes. Event payload detail stays schema-versioned.
groups.evolution: New events use new IDs and payload schemas; transaction-specific events were removed from Core.

groups.name: worker_core_payload_schemas
groups.extension_impossibility: The isolated worker must negotiate, report errors/capabilities/operations/events, transfer immutable frames, and carry the same generic scene/revision/objective envelopes without a second authority.
groups.evolution: FlatBuffers field IDs and 1.0 meanings are immutable; additive fields remain optional and new incompatible semantics use a new schema major.

groups.name: minimum_display_plane
groups.extension_impossibility: One generic color plane is the minimum interoperable render result and is not an estimator, spectrum, polarization, reconstruction, or display-transform commitment.
groups.evolution: Spectral, Stokes, MeasurementBundle, and research planes use independently versioned extensions.

groups.name: core_interfaces
groups.extension_impossibility: The loader, lifecycle, immutable-frame, full-scene fallback, and generic session tables are the interaction grammar that enables clients to evolve independently. The pre-release transaction function was removed from the Scene table.
groups.evolution: Tables may only grow at the tail inside runtime major 1; transaction and future research behavior use separate interface UUIDs.

groups.name: lifecycle_and_envelope_semantics
groups.extension_impossibility: These numeric values define table state machines, concurrency, maturity/state axes, immutable byte interpretation, source carriers, full replacement, and generic session states. They do not select algorithms or expose internal execution policy.
groups.evolution: New semantics append identities; successful meanings and terminal/lifetime behavior of existing values do not change.

pre_release_demotions.reason: Transaction request layout is an Experimental schema carrier, not Core.
Transaction result and renderer strategy evidence must evolve outside Core.
Telemetry providers and limits are optional implementation capabilities.
Transaction events belong to the transaction extension.
Spectral measurement layout requires independent schema evolution.
Polarimetric measurement layout requires independent schema evolution.
Transaction execution is discovered through an extension interface.
Hot-update strategy is renderer implementation evidence.
Partial-rebuild strategy is renderer implementation evidence.
Full-reload strategy is renderer implementation evidence.
Rejected strategy is extension-specific diagnostic evidence.
